surprises.description: Revenue was essentially in line, but the reported loss was materially worse than the preview’s roughly $1.2 million operating-loss base case. The call attributed the $2.6 million loss to member-acquisition marketing; non-GAAP operating results also swung to a $2.1 million loss from a $1.1 million profit a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 consolidated revenue was $22.9 million” and the company reported “a $2.6 million loss” due to member-acquisition marketing spend; “Non-GAAP operating loss was $2.1 million,” versus a $1.1 million profit a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case estimated GAAP operating income of “~$(1.2)M” and EPS of “~$(0.10)”; it also said consensus at “$(0.09) implicitly assumes ~$1M+ of marketing moderation.”

surprises.description: Club-member additions were exceptionally strong: membership grew 65% year over year, and the quarter added more members than any previous quarter. The preview expected an accelerated membership step-up after Q2’s record trial starts, but did not anticipate record quarterly member additions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Club members grew 65% year-over-year,” representing “the largest number of members added in a single quarter in the company's history.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 “delivered record trial starts on doubled marketing” and that “Q3 should show an accelerated step-up.”

surprises.description: Management gave a much clearer 2027 membership-revenue outlook: it expects revenue to rise from about $17 million to more than $30 million, supported by deferred revenue, renewals, and new acquisitions. The preview flagged the relevant “~17.2 / ~30.0+” figures as ambiguous rather than establishing them as revenue guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company projects membership revenue rising from approximately $17 million to more than $30 million in 2027,” supported by “roughly $13 million of existing deferred revenue plus renewals and new acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “~17.2 / ~30.0+” figures “could not be definitively attributed to member counts vs. membership revenue.”

surprises.description: Cash was stronger than the preview’s expected range even though the company continued repurchasing shares. Consolidated cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash reached $8.8 million, above the preview’s base expectation of roughly $5.5–6.5 million, alongside a 256,898-share buyback.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash rose to $8.8 million as of September 30, 2026, up $1.2 million from Q2,” and the company “repurchased 256,898 shares during the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “cash ~$5.5–6.5M” and flagged continued repurchases with low cash as an aggressive posture.

surprises.description: Travelzoo Meta did not launch in the expected Q3 window; the first experiences are now expected in Q4 2026. The preview specifically flagged whether the promised Q3 launch was delivered or slipped.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Travelzoo Meta's first experiences are expected to launch in Q4 2026 as an exclusive benefit of club membership.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Travelzoo META as “promised for Q3'26 as an exclusive club benefit” and asked whether it “launched in Q3 as stated.”

surprises.description: The call added encouraging early acquisition-payback detail: U.S. acquisition cost fell from Q2, while the upfront membership fee plus early transaction revenue exceeds that cost on a gross-revenue basis. However, acquisition cost remained well above its Q1 level, making the evidence positive but not unambiguously so.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Average U.S. club member acquisition cost fell to $54 in Q3 from $62 in Q2,” though it remained above “the $27 level reported in Q1 2026.” Members pay “a $50 annual membership fee upfront” and generate “an average of $15 per member in transaction revenue within 90 days.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified marketing spend and payback as the key debate, noting management would continue investing if it provided “positive ROI and a relatively quick payback,” and said to treat the $1.20 2027 accretion claim as unverified without renewal math.
